summary: The cluster mixes small example contracts (HelloCardano, MembershipToken, PubKey, Preimage, MintingPolicy, Groth16, AMM, AnonymousData, AtomicTransactions, an Aiken-compiled payment splitter) with whole-corpus compiler guards and reports (BooleanOptimizer impact, CCE, CSE tie order, cross-JVM pipeline determinism, source positions). Push-CI cost is dominated by PipelineDeterminismCrossJvmTest (23 s, 100 % in PipelineDeterminismChild.render, F-6/F-23) and the 22 assertion-free BooleanOptimizerImpactTest report tests (7.5 s); AmmTest's 18.5 s in timings.csv is pre-P1 and is already 4.6 s after F-19. Reading found two main-code defects: PubKeyValidator's recursive signer search ignores its argument and never terminates when the key is not the first signatory (C25-5), and Groth16.grothVerify ignores nPublic and any public inputs past vkIC (C25-6). Negative coverage is thin: most AmmValidator, MembershipTokenValidator and HelloCardano rejections have no test, and the existing failure tests accept any failure. No real to-property candidate exists (C4): the only law, AnonymousDataTransactions.open, is three lines and already covered by examples; the AMM k-invariant property is already a property but wraps pure math in Emulator setup (C25-3). The @Compile files are excluded from coverage (F-9); the only real uncovered lines are AmmOffchain.findPool and the resolveSeed failure branch.

findings.claim: The slowest test of the module (23.0 s in timings.csv, F-6) compiles 24 programs under 2-4 configurations twice: once in-process and once in a cold child JVM with -XX:hashCode=2 (100 % in PipelineDeterminismChild.render, F-23). It guards against identity-hash drift anywhere in the pipeline. The bug it was written for (CSE tie order) is also pinned on push by CseTieOrderDeterminismTest (exact hex of SameScopeFieldChains, which is also in this corpus at :144) and by the synthetic core CseDeterminismCrossJvmTest.
findings.action: Tag the test scalus.testing.Benchmark so it runs in nightly.yml, not on push (the repo has no Slow tag; Benchmark is the nightly tag). Alternative if the owner wants it on push: run the child JVM and the in-process render only for the 'release' config (drop 'cce', 'v2' and the legacy configs at :151-169), which roughly halves the time.
findings.coverageRisk: medium: a determinism regression in a non-CSE pass (linker, BooleanOptimizer, MutualRecursionElimination, legacy lowerings) shows up in the nightly run instead of on the push that caused it. The CSE tie-order bug stays guarded on push by CseTieOrderDeterminismTest and CseDeterminismCrossJvmTest.

findings.claim: 'property: k-invariant holds for all valid swaps' creates an Emulator and submits two transactions (create pool, deposit) per case, but never submits a swap: swapQuote is AmmMath.swapResult on the JVM, and the test recomputes the new reserves itself. The validator is not exercised, so the Emulator setup is pure cost. timings.csv shows 5.8 s, but that is pre-P1 (F-19 cut AmmTest from 18.5 to 4.6 s); the remaining cost is the two submitted, script-evaluated txs per case.
findings.action: Rewrite as a property over AmmMath.swapResult(AmmDatum(r0, r1, lp), 997, 1000, t0In, amountIn) with no provider: assert newDatum.r0 * newDatum.r1 >= r0 * r1, 0 <= amountOut < reserveOut, and that the returned datum matches the direction. Keep the same generator and the default minSuccessful: this removes the Emulator, not cases.
findings.coverageRisk: none: the validator's invariant check (AmmValidator.scala:260-263) calls the same AmmMath code, and the submitted swaps at AmmTest.scala:198-251 still run it on-chain

findings.claim: swapGen bounds amountIn by r0 / 10 even when t0In = false (the input reserve is then r1), so it never produces amountIn >= reserveIn (large-swap edge) and almost never the dust case amountOut == 0, which whenever(amountOut > 0) drops anyway. The integer-division edges of swapResult are therefore not exercised.
findings.action: After C25-3 makes the property pure, draw amountIn from the input reserve of the chosen direction, with Gen.frequency over 1 (dust), small, and up to 10x reserveIn; assert amountOut >= 0 for all cases instead of filtering out amountOut == 0.

findings.claim: In all three validators, findSignatureOrFail(sigs) ignores its parameter: it tests signatories.isEmpty and signatories.head (the closure value) and recurses with signatories.tail, so every call sees the same list. With signatories [other, deadbeef] the first call recurses into an identical call forever: on-chain the script runs until the budget is exhausted, and the JVM call PubKeyValidator.validator(...) throws StackOverflowError. 'Signature not found' is unreachable unless the list is empty. Both tests use a single signatory, so the loop never runs. The bloxbean test tree holds a copy of the same file with the same defect.
findings.action: Main code: use sigs in the body of all three findSignatureOrFail (sigs.isEmpty, sigs.head, findSignatureOrFail(sigs.tail)), in both copies. Tests: add to PubKeyValidatorTest a case with signatories [other, deadbeef] (must succeed) and one with [other] (must fail with 'Signature not found'). Optionally drop the unused validator def from the bloxbean copy (only validatorV2/V3 are used there).
findings.verification: The defect is real in all three defs and in both copies. scalus-examples/jvm/src/main/scala/scalus/examples/PubKeyValidator.scala:17-21, 31-36 and 46-51, and bloxbean-cardano-client-lib/src/test/scala/scalus/examples/PubKeyValidator.scala:18-22, 32-37 and 47-52, test and recurse on the closure `signatories`, never on `sigs`. Each call passes `signatories.tail`, but the next call reads `signatories` again. So with a non-empty list whose head is not the key, the recursion never ends. On-chain the script runs until the budget is exhausted. 'Signature not found' is reachable only for an empty list. Current tests use a single matching signatory, so they cannot catch it: PubKeyValidatorTest.scala:38 and bloxbean PlutusScriptEvaluatorTest.scala:32 and :87 use V2/V3. One correction to the JVM symptom: in `validator` (V1) the recursive call is in tail position in a local def, and scalac's tailcalls phase turns it into a loop without @tailrec. So the JVM call hangs forever instead of throwing StackOverflowError. In V2/V3 the call is inside the `trace("nope")(...)` argument, which is not a tail position, so those throw StackOverflowError. Corrected action: use `sigs` in all six bodies. Add the [other, deadbeef] success case and the [other] failure case. Re-pin `flatBytesLen == 120` (PubKeyValidatorTest.scala:53), because the fix changes the V1 script size. Run the JVM-side negative case with a timeout or use the on-chain evaluator, because the unfixed V1 JVM call hangs.

findings.claim: SnarkVerificationKey.nPublic is never read, and derive returns as soon as vk_ic is Nil, ignoring any remaining public inputs. So grothVerify(factorialVK, <the valid 3! proof>, List(561, 3, 999)) returns true: derive([ic1, ic2], [561, 3, 999], ic0) -> derive([ic2], [3, 999], ...) -> derive([], [999], ...) = result. A contract that reads public inputs from a redeemer can be given trailing values that the proof does not bind. Standard Groth16 verifiers reject a public-input list whose length is not nPublic. Parity with the ak-381 source could not be checked offline.
findings.action: Main code: in grothVerify require public.length == vk.nPublic and vkIC.length == nPublic + 1 (or make derive fail when vk_ic is Nil and public is not). Tests: add to Groth16Test a case with one extra public input (must fail both on- and off-chain) and one with a short list ('Invalid input').
findings.verification: `nPublic` is declared at Groth16.scala:50, and no code reads it. The only references to it are the test fixtures Groth16Test.scala:20 and :115. `grothVerify` drops it with the `_` pattern at Groth16.scala:144. `derive` (Groth16.scala:108-118) returns `result` when `vk_ic` is Nil, whatever `public` still holds, and it fails ('Invalid input') only when `public` runs out first. So for factorialVK, which has 3 IC points (2 after the head), List(561, 3, 999) reduces to the same G1 point as List(561, 3), and the valid 3! proof (Groth16Test.scala:57-68) is accepted. Any contract that passes redeemer-supplied public inputs to grothVerify and then reads input index >= nPublic gets a value the proof does not bind. I could not check parity with ak-381 offline. Even if ak-381 behaves the same way, the length check is a missing guard in the Scalus example. The proposed tests are valid additions.

findings.claim: The three FAIL tests pass on any Left from submit: assertSubmitFails ignores the error. A ledger-rule failure (fees, collateral, a missing input) makes them pass without the intended validator check running. initPoolWith also drops both submit results (:445, :450), so a failed pool init would leave the FAIL tests spending a UTxO that does not exist, which also fails, and the tests stay green.
findings.action: Assert the reason: match Left(ScriptFailure(_, logs, _, _)) and require logs to contain 'Deposit: ratio mismatch' (:253-268), 'Swap: slippage exceeded' (:270-286) and 'Pool output must hold r0 of token0' (:288-317); use the helper from C25-8. In initPoolWith assert both submits are Right.

findings.claim: assertSubmitFails is byte-identical in AmmTest and LinkedListTest. ScalusTest has assertScriptFail for build-time failures but nothing for submit-time failures.
findings.action: Add to ScalusTest: assertSubmitFails(provider, tx) and assertSubmitFails(provider, tx, expectedLog: String), the second matching SubmitError.ScriptFailure.logs (or message) like assertScriptFail does. Replace both local copies.

findings.coverageRisk: none: the mint assertion stays in the second test
findings.verification: The test to delete (MembershipTokenTest.scala:40-61) has exactly one assertion: `result.isRight` for the mint tx (:59-60). The surviving test (:63-121) builds the same tx from the same state: a fresh `Emulator.withAddresses(Seq(Party.Alice.address))`, the same `tree.proveMembership(alicePkh)`, the same `MembershipRedeemer.Mint(Data.B(proof))` redeemer, the same tokenName and datum, and the same mint/requireSignatures/payTo/payTo/complete/sign chain against the same `applied` script and env (:64-86). It then asserts `mintResult.isRight` (:88-92) before it burns. Both tests are in jvm/ sources and use the same entry point and config, so no assertion is lost.

findings.claim: Only three AmmValidator rejections have tests (ratio, slippage, drained reserves). Untested: 'Mint: LP delta mismatch' (minting extra LP for free and then redeeming it drains the pool, so this is the most important check), Init without spending the seed, 'Close: pool must be empty', 'Pool output must retain the pool NFT', plus 'Redeem: LP amount exceeds supply' and 'Deposit: zero LP minted'. The last two are not reachable with a balanced Emulator tx: all LP in circulation equals lpSupply, and the ratio check at :218 runs before the zero-LP check for any pool built by deposits.
findings.action: Add one Emulator FAIL test per reachable check, built like the drain test (:288-317, TxBuilder with constMaxBudget, then submit) and asserted by message with C25-8: a deposit that mints lpDelta + 1; a createEmptyPool variant without the seed input; close on a funded pool; a swap whose continuation keeps the reserves but not the NFT. For 'Redeem: LP amount exceeds supply' and 'Deposit: zero LP minted', either skip them or evaluate the script directly on a hand-built ScriptContext, as PreimageExampleTest does.

findings.claim: Besides the non-member case, no MembershipTokenValidator rejection has a test: two required signers (:76), minting 2 tokens or another name (:82-85), deposit below 2 ADA (:93-96), deposit datum for another key (:97-100), burning quantity != 1 (:106), spending the deposit with a Mint redeemer (:129), and spending another member's deposit (the quantityOf check at :125-128).

findings.claim: Three assertions cannot fail: :62-64 re-checks the datum hash that storedUtxo (:34-42) already filtered on, and :65 follows from it (a Hash datum is never inline); :100 compares a pure function call with itself. :80 ignores the submit result. The test title ('the data itself is not on-chain') is never checked: nothing asserts that the tx witness set does not carry the preimage.
findings.action: Delete :62-64 and :100. Assert provider.submit(tx) is Right at :80. Add a check that the witness set does not carry the preimage: tx.witnessSet.plutusData is KeepRaw[TaggedSortedMap[DataHash, KeepRaw[Data]]] (TransactionWitnessSet.scala:31), so assert that its values (unwrapped) do not contain txs.commitment(nonce, data), or that it has no entry for txs.commitmentHash(nonce, data). A builder change that attaches the datum then fails the test.
